items.title: Quantum computing for neuroscience: opportunities beyond classical limits
items.author: Guillaume Dumas
items.content: Some of the least understood phenomena in the brain emerge from interactions between local and global brain states, yet representing their joint activity is a considerable computational challenge. As neuroscience datasets grow and classical methods reach their limits, alternative approaches are needed. Quantum computing, through its novel approach to information processing, may offer a solution.

items.title: Temporal structure tunes the psychedelic experience
items.author: Jake Rogers
items.content: Human brain activity under psilocybin contains latent temporal structure that improves alignment with ongoing context and covaries with the subjective quality of the psychedelic experience.

items.title: Old organoids mimic brain maturation
items.author: Katherine Whalley
items.content: Human brain organoids cultured for more than 5 years reproduce endogenous programmes of postnatal brain maturation and track the passage of time in culture.

items.title: High-performance handwriting brain–computer interfaces
items.author: Yu Qi
items.content: In this Journal Club, Yu Qi discusses a 2021 study that reported a brain–computer interface that used neural activity in the motor cortex to decode attempted handwriting in real time.

items.title: Defining the electrical synapse
items.author: Adam C. Miller
items.content: The mechanisms underlying electrical transmission are often viewed as relatively simple compared with those mediating chemical transmission, yet electrical synapses exhibit dynamic changes in structure and strength. In this Review, Alberto Pereda and Adam Miller examine the structural and molecular bases and complexities of electrical transmission.

items.title: The ventral hippocampus: computations, circuits and functions
items.author: Mazen A. Kheirbek
items.content: Recent years have witnessed major advances in our understanding of the distinct functional and computational roles of the ventral hippocampus (vHPC). Mazen Kheirbek and colleagues examine the state-dependent representation of behaviourally salient information by the vHPC and discuss how its anatomy and circuit connectivity support affective and motivational behaviours.

items.title: Revisiting the olfactory receptor rules
items.author: Darran Yates
items.content: A new study reports that olfactory receptor genes in the mosquito Aedes aegypti can be coexpressed in olfactory neurons and expressed in multiple subtypes of these neurons.
